headline: The Pentagon is considering adding as many as 50 small robot boats to the 10 it already uses to watch the Rio Grande for illegal crossings.
score_reason: Pool score kept: concrete figures and a real pilot, but an expansion that is only under study and a single secondary report.
importance_line: People crossing the Rio Grande could face more constant robot surveillance, and border agencies may get cheap, long-lasting coverage; but the results are the Pentagon's own figures and the expansion is not yet decided.
summary: Outlook India, summarising a Reuters report, says the Pentagon is weighing an expansion of a pilot that uses solar-powered, canoe-sized Seasats "Lightfish" robot boats to spot illegal crossings on the Rio Grande, and may test them in the Gulf of Mexico and later the Pacific. The Pentagon told Reuters the boats helped with an average of 452 detections, 350 apprehensions and 100 turnbacks a month, but for now it is only studying an expansion, not committing to one.
notes: Original outlet Reuters (blocked, HTTP 401); written from Outlook India’s summary of the Reuters report.
